headline_marked: PM calls FY27 budget [[ 'life-friendly' ]] to bring relief to all
headline: PM calls FY27 budget  'life-friendly'  to bring relief to all
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman emphasizes a focus on the general public's welfare, promising relief for the poor and reduced costs for critical medical supplies.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for the current budget to be named the 'life-friendly budget,' stating that the removal of duties on many products has prevented price hikes of essential commodities.

Speaking at the 13th National Parliament session on Monday, the PM emphasized that the government's goal is to shift the economy from the hands of a privileged few to the benefit of the general public.
The PM noted that the economy is under pressure due to rising fuel prices caused by the Middle East crisis, which necessitated a larger budget to address real-world challenges.
Key measures include the waiver of loans up to 10,000 BDT for farmers and the introduction of special cards to resolve daily issues for expatriates.

In the health sector, the government plans to reduce VAT and taxes on critical medical supplies, including dialysis filters, heart stents, and cancer medicines, which could reduce the cost of heart stents by 50%.
The PM also proposed increasing the tax-exempt limit to 400,000 BDT for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 fiscal years and recommended withdrawing the mandatory TIN certificate for property registration.

Regarding education, the government aims to increase the education budget to 5% of the GDP over the next five years and introduce new languages like Mandarin, Japanese, and French as third languages in the curriculum.
The PM also highlighted efforts to recover laundered money from 13 countries through 23 letters sent to foreign governments, and plans for a new industrial park in Bhola following gas discoveries.
caption:
A 'life-friendly' budget? PM Tarique Rahman promises relief for the poor and a 50% drop in heart stent costs.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for the current budget to be named the 'life-friendly budget,' stating that the removal of duties on many products has prevented price hikes of essential commodities.

Speaking at the 13th National Parliament session on Monday, the PM emphasized that the government's goal is to shift the economy from the hands of a privileged few to the benefit of the general public.

The PM noted that the economy is under pressure due to rising fuel prices caused by the Middle East crisis, which necessitated a larger budget to address real-world challenges.

Key measures include the waiver of loans up to 10,000 BDT for farmers and the introduction of special cards to resolve daily issues for expatriates.

In the health sector, the government plans to reduce VAT and taxes on critical medical supplies, including dialysis filters, heart stents, and cancer medicines, which could reduce the cost of heart stents by 50%.

The PM also proposed increasing the tax-exempt limit to 400,000 BDT for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 fiscal years and recommended withdrawing the mandatory TIN certificate for property registration.

Regarding education, the government aims to increase the education budget to 5% of the GDP over the next five years and introduce new languages like Mandarin, Japanese, and French as third languages in the curriculum.

The PM also highlighted efforts to recover laundered money from 13 countries through 23 letters sent to foreign governments, and plans for a new industrial park in Bhola following gas discoveries.

headline: Gold prices drop by ৳3,266 per bhori in Bangladesh
summary: The price of gold has seen a significant decrease, providing relief to buyers in the local market.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have experienced a significant drop, with the price per bhori decreasing by ৳3,266.
This latest price reduction follows a previous decline, marking a trend of decreasing costs for gold jewelry and bullion.
The price adjustment is based on the local market trends and international gold price fluctuations.
Buyers and investors are keeping a close eye on the market to see if prices continue to descend further.
